title: B184 — Adopt Slack (free) + audit every Slack integration across the platform
description:
Adopt a **free** Slack workspace for the lab — even purely as a demo surface it is useful: nearly every tool in the platform ships a Slack integration, and "how would this look in a real org's chat" is part of what the lab demonstrates. Found in the B119 Linear integrations walk (2026-09-25).

**Part 1 — Adopt Slack (free plan).** Create the workspace, record the free-plan limits that shape the design (verify against Slack's current plan page: message-history window, cap on installed apps/integrations — if there is a cap it decides which integrations earn a slot), and connect Linear first.

**Part 2 — Platform-wide audit of Slack integrations.** For every component in the platform, answer: does it have a Slack integration, what does it send or receive, what would it replace or duplicate (alerting goes to **Telegram** today — Alertmanager, the operator), $0 on the free plan, and verdict (adopt / demo-only / skip). Candidates to check, not an assumed list: Linear, Grafana/Alertmanager, Uptime Kuma, GlitchTip, Woodpecker, Argo CD (notifications), Port, Dagster, DataHub, Langfuse, MLflow, Keycloak, GitHub, Figma, the weyland-operator (Slack as a second front door beside Telegram), **Linear initiative updates → a Slack channel** (Settings → Initiatives → Slack notifications; posts only for workspace-level initiatives or ones led by a public team — both true here; pairs with B119.1's OKR check-ins), plus the Linear-directory entries that need Slack (e.g. Graph, Alkemi, Blocks, **Axolo** — a Slack channel per PR synced with its Linear issue; weigh it against a solo reviewer, where a per-PR channel has no one to coordinate).

**Linear → Slack, per team (Team settings → Slack notifications; added 2026-09-26).** Connect a channel for the EMA team and choose events: new project update posted · issue added to the team · issue completed or canceled · issue changes status · comments on issues · issue added to triage. **Sized for the lab's rate (\~30 issues/hour in a working session):** "issue added", "changes status" and "comments" would flood a channel — start with **completed/canceled**, **added to triage** (pairs with the triage rotation) and **project updates** (pairs with initiative updates + Pulse), and record the choice in the channel map. The team intake email (B195) lands issues in the same team, so triage notifications cover those too.

**Part 3 — Wire the adopted set** (secrets sealed, never pasted), one channel map documented, and a demo per integration.

**Deliverable:** the audit table + channel map in a concept doc, the chosen integrations live, runbook + demo (DoD).

**Incident management on Slack — free alternatives (added 2026-09-25).** [incident.io](<http://incident.io>)'s free Basic plan was set aside: the parts that would be used (API/webhooks, MCP, AI summaries/root cause, multiple schedules, private incidents) are all paid. Free, self-hosted candidates to evaluate:

* **Keep** (keephq) — open-source alert management → incidents + workflows; Slack **and Linear** integrations; AI via your own model (Ollama / Anthropic listed). Verify: license, Alertmanager as a source, maintenance activity.
* **OneUptime** (Community Edition, Apache-2.0) — incidents, on-call schedules, status pages, Slack. Verify: API.
* **Runframe** (hosted, **free for up to 5 users**) — incident response, on-call + escalation, status page, **AI post-incident reviews**, Linear follow-ups. The hosted, zero-RAM counterpart to Keep / OneUptime (they give API + own-model control; it costs nothing on mother). Verify on the free tier: Alertmanager as a source, Slack, Linear.
* Ruled out: Grafana OnCall OSS (archived March 2026), Grafana Cloud IRM (paid).
* Cost that matters most: RAM on mother (at its ceiling, B134) — each is another service + database.

**Requirement — alert → Linear follow-up issue (added 2026-09-25).** Nothing in the lab turns an alert into an issue today: Alertmanager/Kuma → Telegram only pages; the operator's B45 sweep dedups incidents in Postgres and sends a Telegram digest but files nothing; GlitchTip → Port makes `glitchtip_issue` catalog entities, not Linear issues. Whatever incident tool is chosen (Keep / OneUptime / Runframe all advertise Linear follow-ups) must close this: a qualifying alert or incident produces a deduplicated Linear issue. Fallbacks if none fits, in order: (a) a small Alertmanager webhook receiver that files the issue (dedups); (b) Linear's pre-installed **Create issues via email** — a team/template intake address + an Alertmanager email receiver (zero new services, but needs outbound SMTP, e.g. a free Gmail app login, and does NOT deduplicate — repeat firings file repeat issues). The team intake address is **enabled** (Team settings → General) and is a **secret**: anyone holding it can file issues unauthenticated, and the repo is public — keep it out of git, store it in a SealedSecret if Alertmanager uses it, and rotate it (the refresh control beside it) if it leaks.

**Requirement — at least ONE pager rotation, exercised (added 2026-09-25, owner).** A solo lab still runs and tests on-call: a rotation between **two Telegram channels** (or Telegram + Slack) with an escalation step, and a test page fired through it so handoff and escalation are proven. Rotation tools and their Linear integrations:

| Tool | Linear integration | Cost | Note |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **OneUptime** | (verify) | free, self-hosted | on-call schedules + escalation built in |
| **Runframe** | Linear follow-ups from incidents | free up to 5 users | on-call + escalation built in |
| **Keep** | Linear provider (create/update issues) | free, open source | rotation via workflows |
| **Pagerly** | sets Linear **triage responsibility** from Slack round-robin rotations | $19/team/mo (30-day trial) | Slack-based |
| **Opsgenie Triage** | rotates Linear **triage responsibility** from Opsgenie schedules | Opsgenie (not used) | Atlassian |
| **Rootly** | auto-creates Linear issues from Slack/Teams incidents | $20/user/mo | full incident platform |
| **SuperDuty** | automatically assigns the on-duty member to Linear **triage** (seen 2026-09-26) | verify | a direct triage-rotation tool — candidate for the exercised rotation |

Linear's own **triage responsibility** (a person who owns incoming Triage) is the Linear-side target these rotate; exercise it too. Preferred path: the rotation lives in the chosen free incident tool; fallback: an Alertmanager route that alternates receivers.

**Telegram ↔ Slack — decide the split (or the deliberate overlap).** An incident tool routes between channels; it is not one. Default proposal to test, not a decision: **Telegram = paging** (phone push; the operator's front door and B45 incident sweep stay there) and **Slack = incident work** (channel per incident, roles, timeline, post-incident review, status page). Overlap is fine where it earns it (e.g. a critical page on Telegram that also opens the Slack incident channel) but it must be designed — the same alert must never just ping twice. Record the final routing table (alert class → Telegram / Slack / both, and why).

Relates B119 (integrations walk), B51 (alerting), B66 (operator), B45 (incident sweep). Detail: [https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md](<https://github.com/edtbl76/weyland-lab/blob/main/docs/backlog.md>)
